footer.aboutText: This is a fun Air Force-style aptitude quiz built around quick reasoning, spatial awareness, map clues, cockpit focus, memory callbacks, and mission-priority questions. It is for entertainment and self-challenge only. It is not an official Air Force test, recruitment exam, military assessment, aviation credential, or training advice.

stageGroups.title: Training Basics
stageGroups.encouragement: You've mastered the basics. Now the pressure increases with a linked training mission, tighter cockpit logic, and details worth remembering.

questions.prompt: Training begins: a jet heads north, then turns right. Which direction is it flying now?
Which instrument shows an aircraft's height above sea level?
If a plane covers 120 kilometres in 30 minutes, what is its average speed?
On a compass, what direction is halfway between north and east?
A warning light flashes during a climb. What is the best first move?
choices: Check the warning and follow procedure

questions.prompt: Which word pair best matches pilot : cockpit?
Which number completes the pattern: 6, 12, 24, 48, ?
Mission Control says wheels up at 14:20. If prep takes 45 minutes, when should prep start?
Which item is most important before takeoff?
Quick trick check: which direction is directly opposite northeast?

stageGroups.title: Base Alpha Mission
stageGroups.encouragement: You handled the training round. This is where the mission starts to feel real: linked clues, fuel checks, and pressure decisions.

questions.prompt: Mission begins at Base Alpha. Fuel starts at 80%. After the first leg it reads 65%. How much fuel was used?
Base Alpha sends you from grid B2 to B5. What changed?
Weather worsens near Base Alpha, but fuel is still safe. What is the best decision?
choices: Ignore the weather because fuel is fine
Inform command and reassess the route

questions.prompt: A radar sweep pings every 4 seconds. How many pings happen in 28 seconds?
You fly east, turn left, then turn left again. Which direction are you facing?
Which cockpit detail is easiest to miss under pressure?
Mission Control reports a weather hazard near Base Alpha. Which message should get highest priority?
Which sequence is the most sensible pre-flight order?
If A = 1, B = 2, and C = 3, what does ACE add up to?
A formation has 5 aircraft. Each aircraft checks in once. How many check-ins are heard?

stageGroups.title: Final Command Assessment
stageGroups.encouragement: This is where most people fail. The final round mixes memory, maps, cockpit focus, and command decisions.

questions.prompt: Earlier in the quiz, which instrument measured altitude?
Earlier at Base Alpha, what was the starting fuel level?
A plane travels 360 kilometres in 90 minutes. What is the average speed?
You are told: Alpha before Bravo, Charlie after Bravo. What order is correct?
Two cockpit readings conflict during a Base Alpha safety check. What should happen next?
choices: Continue if the aircraft still feels stable
Trust the reading you saw first
Ask later if the mission gets harder

questions.prompt: A target marker moves two columns right and one row down from A1. Where does it land?
If ZULU becomes AVMV by shifting each letter forward by one, what does JET become?
A compass heading changes from 045 to 135. How many degrees did it turn?
Mission Control reports fog near the landing area. What is most directly affected?
Final Command: starting at B2, with 65% fuel remaining, your target moves two columns right and one row down. Which coordinate do you report?
